title: docs(qa): re-point dashboards.cross-object-where-engine-path to the post-#33626 contract
body:

_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoH1SLb7yGpZj1NnaFvhbT6W)_
Fixes #35542

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户无感:只改内部测试清单里一条看板跨对象筛选的验收条目,产品行为不变。
- 属于看板跨对象筛选那组工作:测试清单还在按旧规则判,新规则已上线,条目跟着产品走。
- 若写错,下次按清单测试的人会把正确行为判成失败或漏判;纯文档改动,可直接撤回。
- 无。

## What changes
Re-points `dashboards.cross-object-where-engine-path` (revision 1 to 2) in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/dashboards.json` to the post-#33626 contract, per the card's re-point list (`checklist-test` section 5, stale spec; the product is not changed):
- **acceptance[4]**: the 1,000-parent `400 INVALID_FILTER` refusal is replaced by: 1,003 and 21,003 matching parents each answer 200 with the hand count, exactly 1,000 is served, `nope` still answers no rows. The verify text cites the semi-join (`packages/objectql/src/relation-semi-join.ts`) and its pin, and attributes the numbers (count 13, sum 40; 21,003 in 24 ms on PostgreSQL 16 at 92121196) to QA run #35539 as that run's readings.
- **acceptance[5]**: the hop refusal moves from two relationships to four (`CROSS_OBJECT_WHERE_MAX_HOPS = 3` in `cross-object-where.ts`; refusal text "traverses 4 relationships ... up to 3 relationships deep"). The `$not` and `$field` refusals are kept unchanged.
- **title** and **steps 4 and 5** follow those two clauses (step 4 adds the 21,003-parent seed; step 5 probes a four-relationship path).
- **fixtures.knownGaps[0]**: updated rather than dropped, because `fixtures.requires[2]` points at it: #33792 is closed and #35539 measured 5/500 on both paths; the item still scores the engine path only.
- **history**: revision 2 row citing #33626, #35539 and this card.

## Tests
No code changed, so no unit test is owed. Sources re-read at origin/main 8145424b: `cross-object-where.ts` (hop limit 3, structural `multi-hop` refusal), `objectql-strategy.ts` (refusal wording), `relation-filter-lowering.ts` and `relation-semi-join.ts` (subquery on read verbs for a single-valued relation; id cap only where ids are read). The existing pins already carry both behaviours: `packages/rest/src/analytics-nested-relation-filter.test.ts` ("a single-valued match past the id cap is served") and `crossobject-conjunct-refusal.test.ts` (four relationships refused). Both are already in the item's `automated.ref`.

## Acceptance notes
- `source[2]` still reads "content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx (the engine path's orphan rule and the 1000-parent cap)". The doc itself is already current (the subquery with no cap on a SQL datasource; the cap only where ids are read). That source label is outside this claim's declared file surface, so it is left as it is and noted here.
- Step 5's four-relationship path is written with placeholders (`order.R2.R3.R4.name`) because the scratch fixture declares no four-lookup chain. The refusal is structural (segment count, checked before any hop is resolved), so any declared chain will do.
- No changeset: `docs/qa/**` is in no package's `files[]`; `skip-changeset` is declared on this create.

## Verification
Read first: the acceptance[4] verify text in the diff (the riskiest hunk: it changes a refusal into a served answer).
Two-minute check: `pnpm check:platform-checklist` prints `check-platform-checklist: OK — 16 areas, 436 items`.
